intro: How an idea earns its way to production. AI (primarily Claude) supports research, implementation, documentation, and review throughout — but the gates marked below are always human decisions.

stages.title: Idea
stages.description: Write down the problem, who has it, and the riskiest assumption.

stages.title: User & problem research
stages.description: Talk to real users; collect primary evidence and contradictory signals.

stages.title: Business & policy analysis
stages.description: Check unit economics, contracts, terms, data rules, and whether the idea is allowed to exist as imagined.

stages.title: Product specification
stages.description: Define success, non-goals, the MVP boundary, and stop conditions.

stages.title: Architecture
stages.description: Choose the simplest design that current evidence justifies.

stages.title: Small working implementation
stages.description: Build one vertical slice with tests and observable behavior.

stages.title: Technical evaluation
stages.description: Measure against a baseline; inspect failures, not just aggregates.

stages.title: Risk & governance review
stages.description: Review data use, privacy, terms, oversight, and failure consequences before anything public.

stages.title: Preview deployment
stages.description: Ship to a preview environment that cannot hurt anyone.

stages.title: Human verification
stages.description: A person walks the preview, checks the claims, and signs off — or sends it back.

stages.title: Production release
stages.description: Deploy with rollback ready. Never automatic.

stages.title: Monitoring & learning
stages.description: Compare outcomes with hypotheses; feed what actually happened into the next decision.

aiSupport: Claude may support research, implementation, documentation, and review at every stage. It never owns a gate.
